name: Shalom Harlow
milestone_by_age_26: Won the first Vogue/VH1 Model of the Year award in 1995 at age 21, having already appeared on multiple American Vogue covers and walked for top designers.
early_history_summary: Discovered at age 15 by a modeling scout at a Cure concert in Toronto, Harlow began taking modeling lessons and quickly rose in the fashion world. She appeared on her first magazine cover for Canadian publication Fashion in 1993 and on six American Vogue covers between 1993 and 1997. By 1995, she won the first Vogue/VH1 Model of the Year award, cementing her status as a leading model of the 1990s.
family_context_summary: Born in Oshawa, Ontario to David Harlow, a social worker/real estate agent/financial investor, and Sandi Herbert, who worked with developmentally disabled adults. Grew up in a hippie community outside Toronto.
primary_early_advantage_tags: distinctive physical look, scout discovery, Toronto fashion proximity, 1990s supermodel wave
evidence_summary: Harlow was discovered at 15 at a Cure concert in Toronto by scout Anne Sutherland, taking modeling lessons before her first cover at 19. She grew up in a middle-class hippie community in Oshawa, Ontario, with no family connections to fashion. Her rapid rise was driven by her distinctive 5'11" physical look, the 1990s supermodel structural wave, and proximity to the Toronto/New York fashion ecosystem. She appeared on six American Vogue covers between 1993 and 1997 and won the first Vogue/VH1 Model of the Year award in 1995 at age 21.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Oshawa, Ontario; father was a social worker/real estate agent, mother worked with developmentally disabled adults; grew up in a hippie community outside Toronto.
current_position: Continuing modeling career; returned to runway in 2018 after hiatus; featured on Vogue cover in 2023; represented by IMG Models.

trajectory.event: Won the first Vogue/VH1 Model of the Year award, establishing supermodel status.

Named 13th on Forbes' list of the World's Top-Earning Supermodels with estimated $2 million annual earnings.
Returned to runway modeling at Milan Fashion Week for Versace after a six-year hiatus.
Featured on the cover of Vogue alongside major supermodels including Naomi Campbell and Gigi Hadid.

name: Riyoko Ikeda
milestone_by_age_26: Began serializing The Rose of Versailles in 1972 at age 24-25, one of the most influential shōjo manga series ever created, after debuting professionally at 19 in 1967.
early_history_summary: Ikeda began publishing manga while studying philosophy at Tokyo University of Education, debuting in 1967 with 'Bara Yashiki no Shōjo' at age 19. Inspired by Russian literature and Stefan Zweig's biography of Marie Antoinette, she developed a unique style of historical epic manga. In 1972, at age 24, she began serializing The Rose of Versailles, which became one of the most influential shōjo manga of all time.
family_context_summary: Born in Osaka, Japan; father was a manager at a bicycle factory, mother was a full-time housewife. Family moved to Kashiwa before junior high due to father's job transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: literary passion, historical manga innovation, Tokyo manga ecosystem, shōjo manga revolution, social ostracism catalyst
evidence_summary: Ikeda grew up in Osaka in a working-class family; her father managed a bicycle factory and her mother was a housewife. Ostracized by peers as a child, she retreated into books and manga, developing a passion for Russian literature and European history. She began publishing manga while studying philosophy at Tokyo University of Education, debuting at 19 in 1967. Her unique blend of historical epic storytelling with shōjo manga conventions, culminating in The Rose of Versailles (1972), rode the wave of the 1970s shōjo manga revolution.
starting_point: Born in Osaka, Japan; father was a manager at a bicycle factory, mother was a full-time housewife; family moved to Kashiwa following father's job transfer.
current_position: Active as manga artist and opera soprano; received France's Legion of Honour in 2008; Rose of Versailles movie adaptation by studio MAPPA released in January 2025.

trajectory.event: Made professional manga debut with Bara Yashiki no Shōjo while studying philosophy at Tokyo University of Education.
Began serializing The Rose of Versailles in Weekly Margaret, her most famous and influential work.
The Rose of Versailles was adapted into a Takarazuka theatrical production, expanding its cultural reach.
Won the Japan Cartoonists Association Award of Excellence for Orpheus no Mado.
Enrolled in Tokyo College of Music to pursue a career as an opera soprano singer.
Awarded France's Legion of Honour for contributions to Japan's cultural awareness of France.
Rose of Versailles movie adaptation by studio MAPPA released in Japan.

name: Jean Stablinski
milestone_by_age_26: Won Paris-Bourges in 1954 at age 22, his first major professional cycling victory, after turning professional at 21; later won the Vuelta a España in 1958 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born to poor Polish immigrants in the mining region of Nord, France, Stablinski began working in the mines at 14 after his father's death. He won a bicycle in an accordion competition and began racing at 16, turning professional at 21 in 1953. By 1954, he won Paris-Bourges, his first major professional victory, and went on to win the Vuelta a España in 1958 at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born to poor Polish immigrant family in the mining area of Nord, France. Father died in a work accident in 1946, forcing Jean to work in the mine at age 14 to provide income for his family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, mine work, cycling culture of northern France, post-war cycling boom, domestique for Anquetil
evidence_summary: Stablinski was born to poor Polish immigrants in the French mining region; his father died in a mine accident when he was 14, forcing him to work in the mines. He won a bicycle in an accordion competition and began racing at 16, turning professional at 21. His cycling career was built on early immersion in the working-class cycling culture of northern France and the post-war European cycling boom. He won Paris-Bourges at 22 and the Vuelta a España at 26, becoming one of the top professional cyclists of his era.
starting_point: Born to poor Polish immigrant family in the mining area of Nord, France; father died in a mine accident in 1946, forcing Jean to work in the mines at age 14.
current_position: Died on July 22, 2007 at age 75 in Lille, France; final role as former professional cyclist and team manager who discovered Bernard Hinault and Lucien van Impe.

name: Deniz Gezmiş
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Revolutionary Student Union in the summer of 1968 at age 21 and led the occupation of Istanbul University, becoming a nationally known political figure in Turkey.
early_history_summary: Gezmiş became politically active while studying law at Istanbul University, joining the Workers Party of Turkey in 1966. In the summer of 1968, at age 21, he co-founded the Revolutionary Student Union and led the occupation of Istanbul University. He became a nationally known figure through protests against the US 6th Fleet and was arrested multiple times before co-founding the People's Liberation Army of Turkey in 1970.
family_context_summary: Born to Cemil Gezmiş, an education inspector and syndicalist, and Mukaddes Gezmiş, a primary school teacher. Educated in various Turkish cities, spending most of his childhood in Sivas.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an education inspector and syndicalist, which exposed Gezmiş to political and social consciousness from an early age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Istanbul University, student movement, 1968 global protest wave, father's political background, political organizing
evidence_summary: Gezmiş was born to an education inspector father and teacher mother, growing up in various Turkish cities before settling in Istanbul for university. His father's syndicalist background exposed him to political consciousness early. At Istanbul University's law faculty, he became immersed in the leftist student movement of the late 1960s. He founded the Revolutionary Student Union at 21 and led nationally significant protests, riding the wave of the 1968 global student movement. He was executed at 25 in 1972, becoming a lasting symbol of Turkish leftist politics.
starting_point: Born to an education inspector/syndicalist father and primary school teacher mother in Erzurum, Turkey; family moved frequently due to father's job postings.
current_position: Executed on May 6, 1972 at age 25 in Ankara, Turkey; final role as revolutionary leader and founding member of the People's Liberation Army of Turkey (THKO).

trajectory.event: Entered Istanbul University Faculty of Law and joined the Workers Party of Turkey.
Co-founded the Revolutionary Student Union and led the occupation of Istanbul University in June 1968.
Spearheaded protests against the US 6th Fleet in Istanbul, leading to his arrest and national prominence.
Co-founded the People's Liberation Army of Turkey (THKO).
Arrested after a bank robbery and the kidnapping of foreign businessmen.
Executed by hanging in Ankara on May 6, 1972, becoming a lasting symbol of Turkish leftist politics.

name: Shoko Asahara
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Asahara graduated from a school for the blind in 1973, failed university entrance exams, and established a Chinese medicine shop. He founded Aum Shinrikyo in 1984 at age 29; his notoriety came with the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack at age 40.
early_history_summary: Born Chizuo Matsumoto to a poor family of tatami-mat-makers in Kumamoto Prefecture, he had infantile glaucoma and was enrolled in a school for the blind at age 6. He graduated in 1973, failed University of Tokyo entrance exams, and studied acupuncture and traditional Chinese medicine. He established a Chinese medicine shop and married in 1974, living an unremarkable life before founding Aum Shinrikyo in 1984.
family_context_summary: Born to a poor family of tatami-mat-makers in Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan. Had infantile glaucoma from birth, losing all sight in left eye and going partially blind in right eye.
evidence_summary: Asahara was born to a poor tatami-mat-making family in Kumamoto and lost most of his vision due to infantile glaucoma. He attended a school for the blind, graduated in 1973, and failed University of Tokyo entrance exams before turning to acupuncture and Chinese medicine. No material milestone by age 26 was found; he founded Aum Shinrikyo in 1984 at age 29 and gained notoriety with the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack.

name: Josep Lluís Núñez
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Núñez worked as an insurance agent before marrying in 1957 and joining his father-in-law's small building firm. He became FC Barcelona president in 1978 at age 47, building a major construction empire over decades.
early_history_summary: Born in Barakaldo, Basque Country, Núñez moved to Catalonia as an infant when his father, a customs officer, was posted there. He started as an insurance agent and after marrying Maria Lluïsa Navarro in 1957, joined her father's small building firm. Over 20 years, he built Núñez y Navarro into one of the largest construction companies in Spain, before being elected FC Barcelona president in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born in Barakaldo, Basque Country; father was a customs officer. Family settled in Catalonia when he was an infant. Married Maria Lluïsa Navarro in 1957 and joined her father's small building firm.
evidence_summary: Núñez was born in Barakaldo to a customs officer father and moved to Catalonia as an infant. He worked as an insurance agent before marrying in 1957 and joining his father-in-law's small construction firm. No material milestone by age 26 was found; he gradually built the Núñez y Navarro construction company over two decades before being elected FC Barcelona president in 1978 at age 47.

name: Ingemar Johansson
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic silver medal in heavyweight boxing at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 19; turned professional in 1953 and won the European Heavyweight title in 1956 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Johansson began boxing as an amateur in Gothenburg, Sweden, and won a silver medal in the heavyweight division at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 19. He turned professional in 1953 under promoter Edwin Ahlquist, winning the Scandinavian pro title that year. On September 30, 1956, at age 24, he won the European Heavyweight title by KO over Italy's Franco Cavicchi.
family_context_summary: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden. Family background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish national boxing team, Olympics, promoter Edwin Ahlquist, powerful right hand, direct boxing immersion
evidence_summary: Johansson grew up in Gothenburg, Sweden, with limited documentation of his family background in reviewed sources. He won an Olympic silver medal at 19 in 1952, then turned professional under promoter Edwin Ahlquist. His powerful right hand, nicknamed 'toonder and lightning,' propelled him to the Scandinavian and European heavyweight titles by his mid-20s. He later won the world heavyweight championship in 1959 by defeating Floyd Patterson, becoming the fifth heavyweight champion born outside the United States.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on January 30, 2009 at age 76 in Kungsbacka, Sweden; final role as former world heavyweight boxing champion.

Died in Kungsbacka, Sweden.

name: Magnar Solberg
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Solberg's first major accomplishment was helping win the relay at the 1967 Nordic Championships at age 30. He won Olympic gold in the 20km biathlon at the 1968 Grenoble Olympics at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in Soknedal, Norway, Solberg worked as a police officer and competed in biathlon. His first major accomplishment was at the 1967 Nordic Championships at age 30, where he helped win the relay and won bronze in the individual event. He then won Olympic gold in the 20km biathlon at the 1968 Grenoble Olympics at age 31, becoming the oldest Olympic biathlon gold medalist.
family_context_summary: Born in Soknedal, Sør-Trøndelag, Norway. Worked as a police officer.
evidence_summary: Solberg was born in Soknedal, Norway, and worked as a police officer. No material milestone by age 26 was found; his first major accomplishment was at the 1967 Nordic Championships at age 30, and he won Olympic gold at the 1968 Grenoble Olympics at age 31. He remains the only biathlete to successfully defend an Olympic individual title, winning again in 1972 at age 35.

name: Laura Badea-Cârlescu
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in team foil at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 22, followed by World Championship team foil gold in 1994 and individual foil gold in 1995.
early_history_summary: Badea began fencing at age 13 in Bucharest under coach Rodica Popescu, later joining CSA Steaua București. She won an Olympic bronze medal in team foil at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 22. She went on to win World Championship team foil in 1994 and individual foil in 1995, establishing herself as one of the world's top foil fencers before age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania, the youngest of four children. Initially played handball and track and field before turning to fencing at age 13.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Romanian army sports system, CSA Steaua București, coach Rodica Popescu, Maria Vicol, direct fencing immersion
evidence_summary: Badea was born in Bucharest as the youngest of four children, initially playing handball and track before switching to fencing at 13. She trained under Rodica Popescu and Maria Vicol at CSS 1 Bucharest before joining CSA Steaua București, the Romanian army's sports club. The Romanian state sports system provided elite training infrastructure and competitive opportunities. She won Olympic bronze at 22, World Championship gold at 24 and 25, and Olympic gold at 26 in 1996.
starting_point: Born in Bucharest, Romania, the youngest of four children; started fencing at age 13 after initially playing handball and track.
current_position: Retired fencer turned sports administrator; served as President of the Romanian Fencing Federation (2017-2018); inducted into FIE Hall of Fame in 2013; works as fencing coach.

name: Éva Novák-Gerard
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in the 200m breaststroke at the 1948 London Olympics at age 18, set world records in 1950-51, and won Olympic gold and two silver medals at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 22.
early_history_summary: Novák was already an excellent swimmer by age 10, competing with her sister Ilona for the Ferencvárosi TC in Budapest. At 18, she won an Olympic bronze medal in the 200m breaststroke at the 1948 London Olympics. She set world records in 1950-51 and won Olympic gold (4x100m freestyle relay) and two silver medals at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 22.
family_context_summary: Born in Budapest, Hungary. Sister Ilona Novák was also an elite Olympic swimmer, creating a family swimming culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Sister Ilona Novák was an Olympic gold medalist swimmer, providing direct family domain exposure to competitive swimming.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian national swimming program, Ferencvárosi TC, sister Ilona Novák, relay teammate, early swimming start, Budapest swimming infrastructure
evidence_summary: Novák grew up in Budapest in a swimming family; her older sister Ilona was also an elite Olympic swimmer. She was an excellent swimmer by age 10 and joined the Ferencvárosi TC, becoming part of the dominant Hungarian women's swimming program of the era. Her sister Ilona was both a training partner and relay teammate, winning Olympic gold together in 1952. Novák won Olympic bronze at 18, set world records in 1950-51, and won gold and two silvers at the 1952 Olympics at age 22.
starting_point: Born in Budapest, Hungary; older sister Ilona was also an elite Olympic swimmer, creating a family swimming culture.
current_position: Died on June 30, 2005 at age 75 in Brussels, Belgium; final role as former Olympic champion swimmer and eye surgeon.

name: Hakeem Olajuwon
milestone_by_age_26: Drafted #1 overall by the Houston Rockets in the 1984 NBA draft at age 21, became an NBA All-Star as a rookie in 1985, and led the Rockets to the 1986 NBA Finals at age 23.
early_history_summary: Olajuwon grew up in Lagos, Nigeria, playing soccer and handball before switching to basketball at age 15. He enrolled at the University of Houston in 1980, where he helped lead the Cougars to three consecutive Final Four appearances. In 1984, at age 21, he was drafted #1 overall by the Houston Rockets and became an NBA All-Star as a rookie in 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in Lagos, Nigeria. Started as a soccer goalkeeper and handball player before switching to basketball at age 15. Came from a family with no basketball background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: 7-foot frame, soccer footwork, University of Houston, Final Four, coach Guy Lewis, Ralph Sampson Twin Towers, Nigerian outsider, #1 NBA draft pick
evidence_summary: Olajuwon grew up in Lagos, Nigeria, playing soccer and handball before switching to basketball at 15. His soccer goalkeeper background gave him exceptional footwork that later defined his basketball game. He was discovered by Nigerian national team coach Richard Mills and recruited to the University of Houston, where he reached three Final Fours. Despite starting basketball late, his extraordinary 7-foot frame and athletic agility made him the #1 overall NBA draft pick at 21 and an All-Star as a rookie. He later became one of the greatest centers in NBA history, winning back-to-back championships with the Rockets.
starting_point: Born in Lagos, Nigeria; started as a soccer goalkeeper and handball player before switching to basketball at age 15; came from a family with no basketball background.
current_position: Retired NBA legend widely regarded as one of the greatest centers of all time; estimated net worth approximately $200 million; resides in Houston, Texas area.
